open_obligations.what_is_open: A simultaneous heterogeneous-noise Choi--Yuan block expansion whose nonlinear errors satisfy \( |r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) for every eligible \( (g,k)\) on one event with probability tending to one uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The source-level Proposition A.4 in arXiv:2308.02364v1 is a one-block result under iid homoskedastic noise, with failure probability of order \(\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}\). The frozen class instead permits row heteroskedasticity and a growing collection of blocks. Even granting a heterogeneous extension block by block, the union-bound remainder is \(\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}\), which no frozen assumption forces to vanish. The definition of \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) names an upper-bound expression but is not a logical assertion that the estimator remainder obeys it.
open_obligations.attempted: Verified the exact primary-source Proposition A.4 and its probability statement, expanded the eligible-cohort aggregation before taking a maximum, and derived the precise sufficient simultaneous event and its direct union-bound probability. Neither a theorem-level heterogeneous adaptation nor the required block-count/tail relation is present in the frozen core.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For an eligible block \((g,k)\), define
\[
\widehat\tau_{gk}
=\frac{1}{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}
  \bigl(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}\bigr),
\qquad
\tau_{gk}=\frac{1}{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}\tau_{i,g+k},
\]
and let \(b_{gk,q}\) be the expression inside square brackets in the
definition of \(c_{kq}\).  Thus, by that definition,
\[
c_{kq}=\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}b_{gk,q}.
\]
If the exact block expansion is written as
\[
\widehat\tau_{gk}-\tau_{gk}
=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q+r_{gk},
\]
then the definitions of \(\widehat\tau_k\) and
\(\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\) give, by finite-sum rearrangement,
\[
\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q
 \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Since \(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\) and \(s_k>0\), the definition of
\(\rho_{n,k}\) therefore yields
\[
\rho_{n,k}
=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Consequently, on the simultaneous event
\[
\mathcal A_n(C)=
\bigcap_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\bigcap_{g\in E_k}
\bigl\{|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\bigr\},
\]
the triangle inequality and the definition of
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) imply the deterministic bound
\[
\|\rho_n\|_\infty
\le C\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
 \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}
=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
The verified one-block Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 gives, under its own
iid homoskedastic assumptions, a failure probability of order
\(\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}\).  Even if its conclusion were first
extended to the frozen heterogeneous model, a direct union bound would
only give
\[
P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
\le C'
\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
No frozen condition makes the last sum vanish.  Hence the exact vector
identity and the deterministic aggregation bound are proved, but the
claimed uniform stochastic order is not.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) rate for the feasible score loadings that jointly controls \(\widehat c_{kq}-c_{kq}\) and the leave-one-cell-out unit-variance errors at \(o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The variance-replication assumption controls the number of untreated residual replicates, but no frozen assumption or result controls the imputation component \(\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-q)}-m^0_{it}\) or maps the Choi--Yuan block ratios to the required normalized error of \(\widehat c\). Choi--Yuan's feasible variance corollary is homoskedastic and scalar/group-specific, while Choi--Kwon--Liao's feasible CLT is for a fixed group functional and imposes additional nondegeneracy conditions; neither proves a growing \(K\)-by-\(K\) covariance rate for this leave-one-cell-out construction. Declaring the score-loading rate as an assumption would assume the theorem's substantive crux.
open_obligations.attempted: Separated the feasible covariance error into its exact score-loading error, proved the sharp deterministic bound \(2r_n^{\mathrm{score}}+(r_n^{\mathrm{score}})^2\), and propagated it through the diagonal square roots and correlation normalization. Checked the primary low-rank feasible-CLT result, which does not provide the missing growing-dimensional rate for the frozen plug-in estimator.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\) gives
\(\sigma_{uv}=\sigma_u\).  For \(q=(u,v)\), define
\[
\widehat b_{kq}
=\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad
a_{kq}=\frac{c_{kq}\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad
r_n^{\mathrm{score}}
=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
   (\widehat b_{kq}-a_{kq})^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) makes every
division by \(s_k\) valid.  From the definitions of \(s_k\),
\(\Omega_{kk}\), and \(a_{kq}\),
\[
\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}^2
=\frac{1}{s_k^2}\sum_q c_{kq}^2\sigma_u^2
=\frac{\Omega_{kk}}{s_k^2}=1.
\]
The definitions of \(\widehat\Omega\) and \(\Omega\) similarly give
\[
\frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
=\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}\widehat b_{k'q},
\qquad
\frac{\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
=\sum_q a_{kq}a_{k'q}.
\]
Adding and subtracting
\(\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}a_{k'q}\) and applying Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}
&\le
\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2\|a_{k'}\|_2
+\|a_k\|_2\|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2\\
&\quad
+\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2
 \|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2\\
&\le 2r_n^{\mathrm{score}}+(r_n^{\mathrm{score}})^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the first asserted rate follows from the precise missing input
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{score}}
=o_{P_n}\bigl((\log(2K))^{-2}\bigr)
\]
uniformly over the finite slices.  To verify all remaining algebra, put
\[
\delta_n
=\max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}},
\qquad
t_k=\frac{\widehat s_k}{s_k}.
\]
The diagonal case gives \(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_n\); since \(t_k\ge0\),
\[
|t_k-1|=\frac{|t_k^2-1|}{t_k+1}\le\delta_n.
\]
If \(\delta_n=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\), then uniformly in \(k,k'\),
\(t_kt_{k'}=1+o_{P_n}(1)\).  Since every correlation satisfies
\(|\Sigma_{kk'}|\le1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}-\Sigma_{kk'}|
&\le
\frac{\delta_n}{t_kt_{k'}}
+|\Sigma_{kk'}|
 \left|\frac{1}{t_kt_{k'}}-1\right|\\
&=o_{P_n}\bigl((\log(2K))^{-2}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the claimed covariance, scale, and correlation implications
conditional on the score-loading rate.  The frozen assumptions do not
control the leave-one-cell-out imputation contamination in
\(\widehat e_{it}\), nor do they transport the block perturbation ratios
to \(\widehat c_{kq}-c_{kq}\) in this normalized rowwise
\(\ell_2\) norm.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The uniform feasible transfer from the oracle influence maximum to the studentized conditional multiplier band.
open_obligations.obstruction: This transfer requires the unresolved uniform nonlinear-remainder rate and feasible covariance rate. It also requires theorem-granularity logical nodes for high-dimensional Gaussian approximation, Gaussian anti-concentration, and Gaussian covariance comparison. The bibliography record alone is not a proof premise. The frozen cell-leverage and sub-Gaussian conditions identify the inputs to such results, but they do not themselves state their conclusions.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced the multiplier law exactly, conditional on the data, to the maximum of an \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\) vector; derived the explicit perturbation from estimated studentization and the nonlinear remainder; and verified that the claimed upstream logarithmic rates are sufficient for anti-concentration. The argument cannot be completed while those upstream rates and classical theorem nodes are absent.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Define the oracle linear process and feasible multiplier coordinates by
\[
S_{n,k}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
 a_{kq}\frac{e_q}{\sigma_q},
\qquad
\widehat Z_{n,k}^{\xi}
=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
 \frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_k}\xi_q.
\]
Conditional on \(Y\), the multiplier vector is exactly Gaussian and
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 \widehat Z_{n,k}^{\xi},\widehat Z_{n,k'}^{\xi}\mid Y\right)
=\frac{\sum_q\widehat c_{kq}\widehat c_{k'q}
 \widehat\sigma_u^2}{\widehat s_k\widehat s_{k'}}
=\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}.
\]
Hence no separate multiplier central limit theorem is needed after
consistent estimation of the full covariance: conditionally,
\(W_n^\xi\) is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of a
\(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\) vector.

For the feasible statistic, put \(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  The exact
influence identity gives
\[
\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}
=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|t_k^{-1}(S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k})|.
\]
On the event \(\max_k|t_k-1|\le\gamma_n<1\), the reverse triangle
inequality implies
\[
\left|
 \max_k|t_k^{-1}(S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k})|-
 \max_k|S_{n,k}|
\right|
\le
\frac{\gamma_n}{1-\gamma_n}\max_k|S_{n,k}|
+\frac{\|\rho_n\|_\infty}{1-\gamma_n}.
\]
Independence, centeredness, the sub-Gaussian bound, and
\(\sum_q a_{kq}^2=1\) give
\(\max_k|S_{n,k}|=O_{P_n}(\sqrt{\log(2K)})\) by the exponential Markov
inequality and a union bound.  Therefore the asserted scale rate
\(\gamma_n=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-1})\) makes the first term
\(o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-1/2})\).  The asserted influence rate together
with
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) makes the second term
of the same smaller order after choosing a slowly diverging tightness
constant.  A theorem-granularity Gaussian approximation and Gaussian
anti-concentration result would then transfer the oracle process to
\(N(0,\Sigma_n)\), while a Gaussian covariance-comparison result and
\(\|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) would transfer its law to the exact
conditional multiplier law above.  These last classical results are
not declared logical nodes, and the two required upstream stochastic
rates remain unproved in the frozen core.
